content.text: When you touch a metal spoon that's been sitting in a hot drink, it feels hot. The heat has travelled through the solid metal by a process called conduction. This is one of the three main ways heat can be transferred.

Conduction is the transfer of thermal energy through a material by the vibration of particles. Energy passes from particle to particle without the particles themselves changing position. It is the main method of heat transfer in solids.

A metal bench feels colder than a wooden bench at the same temperature because metal conducts heat away from your body faster -- not because it is actually at a lower temperature. Both are at the same temperature; metal just has a higher thermal conductivity.
Conduction works best in solids (especially metals). In metals, free electrons as well as vibrating atoms transfer energy, making conduction much faster than in non-metals.

content.text: Explain why a metal spoon in a hot drink feels hotter than a wooden spoon.

Metal has free electrons that transfer heat energy quickly from the hot end (in the drink) to the cool end (your hand). Wood is an insulator with no free electrons; heat travels slowly through it by particle vibration only. So the metal spoon conducts heat to your hand much faster.

Why does a tile floor feel colder than a carpet at the same temperature?
Tile is a better conductor than carpet:
When you stand on tile, it conducts heat away from your feet quickly
Carpet is an insulator (contains trapped air) and conducts heat away slowly
Both are at room temperature, but the tile removes heat from your feet faster
Your feet lose heat faster on the tile, making it feel colder

When one end is heated, these free electrons gain kinetic energy and travel quickly to cooler regions, transferring energy by colliding with metal ions. Plastics have no free electrons, so energy can only be transferred slowly through particle vibrations. (explanation with physics reasoning)
The copper rod's far end gets hot first.

Copper has a much higher thermal conductivity (401 W/m·K) than glass (1.0 W/m·K) because copper has free electrons that transfer energy rapidly. Glass relies only on slow particle vibrations. (comparison)
A sleeping bag traps a thick layer of air in its filling.

Air is a very poor conductor of heat (k = 0.025 W/m·K). The trapped air pockets prevent your body heat from conducting away quickly, keeping you warm. The bag does not generate heat; it reduces the rate of heat loss from your body. (explanation with physics reasoning)
Metal bottoms conduct heat quickly from the stove to the food
(high thermal conductivity). Plastic handles are insulators (low thermal conductivity), so heat travels slowly along them, protecting your hand. (explanation with physics reasoning)
Fluffed-up feathers trap a thicker layer of air
close to the bird's body. Air is a poor conductor, so the trapped air reduces heat loss from the bird's body by conduction. (explanation with physics reasoning)
Double-glazed windows have a gap of air or argon gas between two panes.
Air and argon are poor conductors, so the gas layer greatly reduces heat conduction through the window compared to a single pane of glass. (explanation with physics reasoning)
